_comment: flint-vs-knfsd differential floors. A regression is the RATIO falling,
not the MiB/s falling: the rig is a 2-vCPU VM on a laptop and its
absolute numbers are not comparable across time. knfsd is measured in
the same session, interleaved per rep, so rig drift is common-mode.
PROVENANCE. Two independent full runs, 2026-08-31, on lima
flint-nfs-client (Ubuntu 6.8.0 aarch64, 2 vCPU / 2 GiB), each on a
FRESHLY REBOOTED VM with the host idle (the earlier same-day rig
carried a poisoned uncommittable NFS folio and load 65 — reboot is
part of the procedure now). flint-pnfs-mds built from v1.43.0
(8708a5f5), mode standalone, sqlite state backend, SPLICE ON BY
DEFAULT — this baseline is what retired the 2026-08-28 one (read
0.459 / write 0.605 / meta 0.665) after the write campaign, the
splice default-on, and the small-file work landed.
dimension   run1    run2    ratio drift
Floors are the LOWER of the two runs, so a baseline fluke cannot make
the gate stricter than the rig can sustain. read ratio > 1.0 is real:
with splice on, flint's read path outruns knfsd on this rig, and the
floor now HOLDS that.
TOLERANCE 0.15, unchanged. Observed run-to-run ratio spread: ~1-3%
for write/meta (15% is 5x+ noise, as before) but 7.3% for read —
the read margin is now ~2x observed noise, not 5x. If the read leg
starts crying wolf, add runs and re-derive — do not widen the band.
Effective floors: read 1.008, write 0.774, meta 0.632.
FALSIFIABILITY (this is what makes the numbers above mean anything):
the deliberately crippled mount (rsize/wsize 4096) scored read
0.120/0.119 and write 0.243/0.230 across the two runs, against
floors of 1.008 and 0.774. The gate sees it. The knfsd control
stayed inside the band on the crippled runs, so the collapse is the
server arm, not the rig. meta (0.745/0.653) is barely affected by
rsize and is NOT expected to fail on the crippled arm.
A CLAIM ABOUT FLINT'S SPEED, now: read 1.186-1.280 means the
userspace server's read path beats the in-kernel one on this rig
with splice on. write 0.91 and meta 0.74 are floors to hold AND
gaps still open — parity-ish on write, a real deficit on meta
(the stat-consolidation lever is un-pulled).
CONTROL HEALTH. control_mib_s records what KNFSD measured when this
baseline was taken (means of the two runs: read 1636/1481,
write 752/617, meta 1337/1284 ops/s). knfsd does not change when
flint does, so if the control drifts outside +/-30% the RIG moved,
and a ratio from it is not comparable. That matters because
saturation compresses the ratio toward 1.0: a contended run reports
a BETTER ratio and would hide a regression. Observed twice now:
a runaway logind (2026-08-28, read 'improved' 0.46 -> 0.93) and a
reclaim-wedged VM (2026-08-31, load 65 from one stranded folio).
WEDGE WARNING for the crippled arm: wsize=4096 buffered writes on
the loopback rig can deadlock the whole VM under memory pressure
(client reclaim needs a COMMIT the server cannot answer while its
own writes sit in reclaim). If the falsifiability arm hangs for
tens of minutes with VM load climbing and zero CPU: reboot the VM,
re-stage /tmp/flint-pnfs-mds-vm, rerun. knfsd wedges the same way.
